content.text:
Fixed in `target-app/src/App.tsx`.

The toggle only ever lived in React state, so every reload started from `useState(false)`. Two changes:

- `readStoredTheme()` reads `localStorage` and is passed as the lazy initializer to `useState`, so the first render already has the right theme (no light-then-dark flip on mount).
- The existing `useEffect` that writes `document.body.dataset.theme` now also writes the value to `localStorage`, keeping the DOM and storage in sync from one place — including the initial mount.

Both accesses are wrapped in `try/catch`: `localStorage` throws outright in some privacy configurations, and there the app falls back to light mode rather than crashing.

Kane's browser run went green after the second edit — `darkmode_test.md` step "Verify dark mode survived" now passes.
